tasks.short: Observe equipment and notify operators of malfunctions

steps.what: Observe equipment operations and recognise signs of malfunctions
Notify the operator of observed malfunctions and clarify location and urgency

tasks.design: Keep equipment observation and direct operator notification with the helper. Existing instructions in {DOCS} may support recognition, but no sensor or structured malfunction signal is assumed to replace attention.
tasks.previous_blocker: Helpers notice physical cues that may not be instrumented.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change to live malfunction recognition is supplied.
tasks.still_hard: Unfamiliar sounds, smells or movement require prompt judgement and escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a new unsafe condition and communicate it clearly.
tasks.altitude: Observation and escalation duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Which conditions require an immediate stop or specialist response

evidence.claim: Retaining observation and notification in full is an E1 task design; generic production analytics do not establish this task's saving.

assumptions: Boundary is helper observation and notification; operator diagnosis and repair are outside it.
No structured malfunction code or sensor producer is assumed; helper observation remains counted in s1.
No new system or upkeep is proposed, so native configuration is unnecessary.
unknowns: Equipment hazards and local escalation rules
research_questions: Which observable cues require immediate notification regardless of instrument readings?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no upkeep give net=0; no free malfunction feed replaces physical observation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Separate products by weight, grade, size or composition

steps.what: Check product weight, grade, size or composition against sorting instructions
Separate products into the appropriate physical groups and isolate uncertain items

tasks.design: Keep assessment and physical separation with the helper. Sorting instructions in {DOCS} support the work, but a camera classifier alone does not move products or prove their composition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product handling and suitable measurements remain necessary.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated sorter or composition-measurement system is established for this setting.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed materials and borderline grades need judgement and escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Isolate uncertain products rather than forcing an unjustified category.
tasks.altitude: Sorting and handling duties remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Inspekto supports visual inspection, but the supplied capability does not establish physical separation by weight or material composition.
Retaining all product assessment and handling is an E1 design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is helper classification checks and physical separation, excluding specialist laboratory tests.
Helper produces category judgements during s1; no free weight, composition or grade feed is assumed.
No new sorting hardware or software is proposed, so native configuration and incremental upkeep are zero.
unknowns: Product types, measurement methods and category tolerances
research_questions: Which categories cannot be determined with available tools and need specialist review?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. Visual classification is not credited as physical handling automation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read gauges or charts and record obtained data

steps.what: Read gauges or charts and capture values with equipment, unit and time
Enter obtained readings into the designated log
Check recorded readings and clarify missing, implausible or unreadable values

tasks.design: Configure a native reading form in {OPS_SYSTEM} with reusable equipment and unit fields. Keep reading and initial value capture fully counted, and reduce only repeated log labels and duplicate entry; no sensor feed or model reading is presumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper log structure can require repeated identifiers and later duplicate entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse selected equipment and units while preserving actual observation.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable scales and inconsistent units require a person to check the instrument.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that an apparently valid number may be the wrong reading.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive log entry, with unchanged measurement responsibility.

evidence.claim: Native manual reading forms and the proposed entry saving are E1 design assumptions; no connected gauge is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is manual gauge/chart observation and its primary reading log. This task owns meter-reading capture; the separate production-information task does not recapture or claim savings on those same values.

Helper in s1 produces equipment identifier, gauge or chart reference, value, unit, observation time and uncertainty. All reading and first capture remain in 45 full hours; retained s2 time includes equipment selection and input correction.
Missing identifiers, unreadable values or unavailable devices require manual log entry within retained s2 and s3 time. No automatic plausibility rule substitutes for s3 review.
Test native forms before code. Savings apply only if redundant labels or copying exist; three focal upkeep hours cover form and unit-list checks.
unknowns: Equipment identifiers and native form support
research_questions: Can the form halve repetitive entry without reducing reading or verification time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=82.5, gross=17.5 minus 3 upkeep gives net=14.5. High assumes repeat labels and copying; low assumes only 3 entry hours removable. Reading 45 and checking 20 remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record tested-product counts and production dates and times

steps.what: Determine tested-product counts and production dates and times and capture their source
Record production information and verify counts, dates and times against source facts

tasks.design: Use a native production form in {OPS_SYSTEM} to reuse work-order labels and record captured counts and event times once. Keep counting, identifying the actual production event and verifying the final record human; entry time is never substituted for the event time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Production forms may repeat work-order labels and previously captured facts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse record context and avoid copying between forms.
tasks.still_hard: Rework, partial batches and uncertain event times require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Check what was actually tested or produced rather than accept a convenient total.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate recording, with unchanged responsibility for source facts.

reach.learn: How to distinguish test counts, output counts and rework

evidence.claim: Native production record reuse and the proposed recording saving are E1 design assumptions, not a measured helper case.

assumptions: Boundary here is tested-product counts and production event dates/times. Meter readings are an alternative example in the statement and are owned by task 12715; no meter-reading labour or saving is added here.

Helper in s1 produces work-order reference, count type, count value, batch reference, event date/time and source or uncertainty; its full 60 hours include counting and first capture. Existing planning staff produce unchanged work-order identifiers.
Retained s2 time includes field entry, verifying counts and actual event time, and manual form fallback if context cannot be reused. No automatic count or event-time producer is assumed.
Test native forms before code. Three focal upkeep hours cover form, field and access checks; gauge-log upkeep is separately owned and not repeated here.
unknowns: Duplicate recording share and batch identification quality
Required count definitions and time precision
research_questions: Can work-order reuse halve recording effort after all source verification and exceptions?

already_counted.description: Entry, verification and manual form fallback

incremental.description: Maintain production-information form and field controls

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 minus 3 upkeep gives net=17. High requires duplicate production recording; low assumes only 3 hours removable. Source capture retains 60 hours and meter-reading work is excluded to prevent duplication.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Record entry may shrink while observation, counting, sorting and physical work remain central.
reach: Production supervisor: escalation and batch reconciliation
role.ambitious_version: Support production with trustworthy source facts and prompt escalation while keeping physical observation and handling visible.
